methods.name: Push
methods.description:
Push a plugin archive to install or upgrade it.
 Creates the plugin if it does not exist, or installs a new version of an
 existing plugin; pushing the archive already installed changes nothing.
 The archive is a plugin folder in the Agent Plugins, Cursor, Claude Code
 or Codex layout; the response's status lists what the plugin holds and
 what was skipped.

methods.name: CreateArtifactUploadUrl
methods.description:
Mint a short-lived, single-use upload URL for staging a plugin archive
 that exceeds the gRPC message-size cap (10MB). Flow:

 1. createArtifactUploadUrl(org, size_bytes) → { url, artifact_upload_ref }
 2. HTTP PUT the ZIP bytes to url
 3. push(PushPluginRequest{ artifact_upload_ref })

methods.name: UpdateVisibility
methods.description:
Update the visibility of a plugin.
 Only modifies metadata.visibility.

methods.name: Delete
methods.description:
Delete a plugin, its evals included.
 Refused while an agent of the organization lists it; the error names the
 agents. Refused while one of its evals is pending or running: cancel that
 eval first.

methods.name: ListTools
methods.description:
List the tools one of a plugin's MCP servers offers now, signed in as
 the caller. Nothing is stored.

 Errors:
 - FAILED_PRECONDITION: a key the server needs is in none of the caller's
   vaults, or the server needs a sign-in the caller has not made
 - NOT_FOUND: the plugin, or the server in it, does not exist

methods.name: Get
methods.description: Get a single plugin by ID.

methods.name: GetByReference
methods.description:
Get a plugin by API resource reference with version support.

 Version resolution (via ApiResourceReference.version field):
 - Empty/"latest" → Returns the installed version
 - Tag name (the manifest version, e.g. "1.2.0") → Resolves to the version holding this tag
 - SHA-256 digest (64 hex chars) → Returns the exact immutable version

methods.name: GetArtifact
methods.description:
Download a plugin archive from storage by its storage key.
 Returns the ZIP file the plugin was installed from.

methods.name: GetArtifactDownloadUrl
methods.description:
Mint a URL for downloading a plugin archive over HTTP.

 Preferred over getArtifact for anything that might exceed the gRPC
 message-size cap (10MB): the bytes ride HTTP. Callers try this first and
 fall back to getArtifact against servers that predate it (UNIMPLEMENTED).

methods.name: ListVersions
methods.description:
List version history for a plugin.

 Returns every installed version ordered by push time (newest first), with
 its digest, tag, actor and archive storage key.

methodTypes.name: PushPluginRequest
methodTypes.description:
PushPluginRequest installs or upgrades a plugin from its archive.
 Creates the plugin if it does not exist, or installs a new version of an
 existing plugin; pushing the archive already installed changes nothing.

 The archive travels one of two ways (exactly one must be set):
 - artifact: inline ZIP bytes, bounded by the gRPC message-size cap (10MB).
 - artifact_upload_ref: a reference to bytes staged via
   createArtifactUploadUrl() + HTTP PUT, for archives above the cap.

fields.name: Org
fields.description: Organization the plugin is installed into.

fields.name: Artifact
fields.description:
The plugin package as a ZIP archive: the plugin folder with its manifest,
 skills/, mcp.json, agents/ and hooks/ at the archive root.

 Mutually exclusive with artifact_upload_ref (see the message comment).

fields.name: ArtifactUploadRef
fields.description:
Reference to an archive staged via createArtifactUploadUrl().

 Mutually exclusive with artifact (see the message comment).

fields.name: Visibility
fields.description:
Visibility for the plugin. Unspecified means the kind's default
 (organization).

fields.name: Message
fields.description:
Optional human-readable message describing this version, kept in
 metadata.version.message for the version history.

methodTypes.name: CreatePluginArtifactUploadUrlRequest
methodTypes.description:
CreatePluginArtifactUploadUrlRequest asks the server to mint a staging
 slot for a plugin archive too large to travel inline.

fields.name: Org
fields.description:
Organization that will own the plugin (the authorization scope; the
 caller needs the same can_create_plugin permission push requires).

fields.name: SizeBytes
fields.description:
Declared size of the archive in bytes; an over-limit declaration is
 refused before any bytes move.

methodTypes.name: PluginArtifactUploadUrl
methodTypes.description:
PluginArtifactUploadUrl is a short-lived, single-use capability for
 staging a plugin archive over HTTP.

fields.name: Url
fields.description: URL to PUT the archive bytes to. Content-Type: application/zip.

fields.name: ArtifactUploadRef
fields.description:
Opaque reference to pass as PushPluginRequest.artifact_upload_ref after
 the PUT succeeds. Single-use; invalid after the push consumes it or the
 TTL lapses.

fields.name: TtlSeconds
fields.description: Time-to-live for the upload URL in seconds.

methodTypes.name: UpdateVisibilityInput
methodTypes.description:
Input for updating the visibility of any API resource.

 Used by resource-specific command controllers to change visibility.
 Each controller's updateVisibility RPC accepts this shared input
 and returns the full updated resource.

 Visibility transitions trigger FGA tuple management in Cloud mode. Each
 level maps to exactly one tuple shape; on a transition the tuple for the
 old level is removed and the tuple for the new level is created:
 - PRIVATE:  no visibility tuple (owner + explicit grants only)
 - ORG:      resource#viewer@organization:<org>#viewer
 - CHILD_ORGS: resource#child_org_viewer@organization:<org>#child_org_viewer

 Not all resources support all visibility levels — the supported set is
 declared per kind via VisibilityConfig in kind_meta:
 - Blueprints (agent, skill, plugin):
     PRIVATE, ORG, or CHILD_ORGS
 - Org-only kinds (vault):
     PRIVATE or ORG (never CHILD_ORGS — tenant isolation)

 visibility_public is refused for every kind (INVALID_ARGUMENT naming the
 supported levels); the level is retired.

fields.name: ResourceId
fields.description: ID of the resource whose visibility is being updated.

fields.name: Visibility
fields.description:
The new visibility setting for the resource.
 Must not be unspecified (0). Valid values depend on resource kind —
 see the VisibilityConfig in the kind's kind_meta.

methodTypes.name: ListPluginToolsInput
methodTypes.description:
ListPluginToolsInput names one MCP server of an installed plugin whose
 tools to list.

fields.name: PluginId
fields.description: System-generated ID of the plugin.

fields.name: Server
fields.description: The server's name in the plugin (an McpServerEntry name).

fields.name: Org
fields.description:
Organization whose runner reaches the server; the caller's My vault in
 it supplies the server's keys and sign-in.

methodTypes.name: ListPluginToolsOutput
methodTypes.description: ListPluginToolsOutput lists the tools one MCP server offers now.

fields.name: Tools
fields.description: The tools, in the order the server listed them.

methodTypes.name: ApiResourceReference
methodTypes.description:
Generic reference to any API resource by org and slug.
 Used across resources to reference other resources (e.g., Vault, Agent, Skill).
 Canonical format: "org/slug" (e.g., "acme/web-search", "acme/my-agent").

 Every reference in a resource's spec is checked when the resource is
 written: the target must exist, and a target in another organization
 must be one the writing organization's parent shares with its child
 organizations (visibility_child_orgs) to be referenced at all. A blueprint may not be
 more visible than the skills, plugins and agents it references, so
 what a person can run they can also read. A reference that fails the
 check is refused at write, never at run.

fields.name: Org
fields.description:
Organization that owns the referenced resource, by slug or id.

 When non-empty: an organization slug (lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens,
 starts with a letter, 2-63 characters; e.g. "stigmer", "acme-corp") or an
 organization id (org_<ulid>). The server stores the id, so a stored
 reference keeps pointing at its organization across a rename.

 When empty: the reference is relative — the server resolves it to the parent
 resource's organization at write time. All stored and returned references
 always have org populated (absolute form, the id).

 Use empty org for same-org references (the common case).
 An explicit other org is accepted only when that organization is your
 organization's parent and shares the resource with its children
 (visibility_child_orgs).

fields.name: Kind
fields.description: Kind of the referenced resource (e.g., SKILL, AGENT, PLUGIN).

fields.name: Slug
fields.description:
Resource slug (user-friendly identifier, unique within org).
 Format: lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens, must start with a letter
 and end with a letter or digit (e.g., "web-search", "code-reviewer").
 Length: 2-63 characters.

fields.name: Version
fields.description:
Version of the resource (optional, only applicable to versioned resources like Skills).
 Supports three formats:
 1. Empty/unset → Resolves to "latest" (most recent version)
 2. Tag name → Resolves to version with this tag (e.g., "stable", "v1.0")
 3. Exact hash → Immutable reference to specific version (e.g., "abc123...")

 Default behavior: Empty means "latest" (current version).
 This field is ignored for non-versioned resources.

 Examples:
 - version: ""           → Use latest version
 - version: "latest"     → Use latest version (explicit)
 - version: "stable"     → Use version tagged as "stable"
 - version: "v1.0"       → Use version tagged as "v1.0"
 - version: "abc123..."  → Use exact version with this hash (immutable)

methodTypes.name: GetArtifactRequest
methodTypes.description: GetArtifactRequest requests download of a plugin archive by storage key.

fields.name: ArtifactStorageKey
fields.description: The archive storage key from plugin.status.artifact_storage_key.

fields.name: Artifact
fields.description: The plugin archive as a ZIP file (binary content).

methodTypes.name: PluginArtifactDownloadUrl
methodTypes.description:
PluginArtifactDownloadUrl provides a URL for downloading a plugin archive
 over HTTP.

fields.name: Url
fields.description: URL to download the archive ZIP via HTTP GET.

fields.name: TtlSeconds
fields.description: Time-to-live for the download URL in seconds; 0 means no expiry.

fields.name: SizeBytes
fields.description: Size of the archive ZIP in bytes.

methodTypes.name: ListPluginVersionsInput
methodTypes.description: ListPluginVersionsInput requests the version history for a plugin.

fields.name: Org
fields.description: Organization that owns the plugin.

fields.name: Slug
fields.description: Plugin slug (unique within the organization).

fields.name: PageToken
fields.description: Opaque token for cursor-based pagination. Empty for the first page.

fields.name: PageSize
fields.description: Maximum number of versions to return per page. Default is 50.

methodTypes.name: ListPluginVersionsResponse
methodTypes.description: ListPluginVersionsResponse is a page of plugin version history.

fields.name: Versions
fields.description: Versions, newest first.

fields.name: NextPageToken
fields.description: Token for the next page. Empty when no more pages exist.

fields.name: TotalCount
fields.description: Total number of versions across all pages.

enumTypes.name: ApiResourceVisibility
enumTypes.description:
Visibility controls who can access an API resource.
 This is orthogonal to ownership - visibility is about access control,
 while ownership (org) determines who manages the resource.

 Key distinction:
 - Ownership: Which organization controls/manages the resource
 - Visibility: Who can access/use the resource

 All resources belong to an organization. Visibility determines which
 users, inside that organization or in its child organizations, can read
 the resource. No level reaches every
 account on the server.

 The visibility levels map to FGA tuples:
 - PRIVATE: no additional viewer tuples (owner-only access)
 - ORG: resource#viewer@organization:<org>#viewer tuple (everyone in the
   org — the org role hierarchy flows downward, so owners, admins, members
   AND read-only viewers all satisfy the organization#viewer userset)
 - CHILD_ORGS: resource#child_org_viewer@organization:<org>#child_org_viewer
   (everyone in every child organization of the owning organization)
 - PUBLIC: retired; see the value's own comment.

values.name: visibility_private
values.description:
Only the owner, explicitly granted principals, and — for blueprint kinds
 in the cloud edition — org admins can access.
 This is the default for personal and run-scoped resources.

 Org admins count as owners of blueprint kinds (agent, agent_share,
 skill, plugin), so a private blueprint stays
 manageable — and visible — to its org's admins. Personal kinds
 (sessions) stay creator-only.

values.name: visibility_public
values.description:
Retired. This level made a resource readable to every account on the
 server; it is refused at create and at updateVisibility for every kind,
 and every stored row that held it has been moved to visibility_org.
 Sharing across organizations happens through plugins (a copy is
 installed and owned) or, from a parent organization to its children,
 through visibility_child_orgs.

values.name: visibility_org
values.description:
Everyone in the owning organization can access (read) this resource —
 all org roles including read-only viewers (the role SSO auto-provisioning
 grants by default). Running or otherwise spending against the resource
 still requires the org-level member-or-guest permissions
 (can_create_session / can_create_run_in); org visibility widens
 read, never spend.

 FGA tuple: resource#viewer@organization:<org>#viewer
 (The tuple once targeted organization#member, which
 excluded viewer-role users; the authorization model no longer admits
 that shape.)

values.name: visibility_child_orgs
values.description:
Everyone in every child organization of the owning organization can
 read and run this resource: the shared catalog an organization offers
 the organizations under it (spec.parent_org). Child organizations
 created later gain access automatically, and no other organization
 does. Instances, sessions, runs and vaults are never shared
 this way: each child runs the shared blueprint inside its own boundary.

 Only valid for blueprint kinds with supports_child_orgs: true, and only
 in an organization that is not itself a child.

 FGA tuple: resource#child_org_viewer@organization:<org>#child_org_viewer

values.name: api_resource_version
values.description: Immutable version record tracking changes to an API resource.

values.name: iam_policy
values.description: Role-based access control policy for granting permissions on resources.

values.name: identity_account
values.description: User account in the identity system.

values.name: api_key
values.description: Credential for programmatic API access.

values.name: invitation
values.description: Shareable link for joining an organization with a configurable role.

values.name: identity_provider
values.description: External identity provider for federated authentication.

values.name: oauth_app
values.description: Registered OAuth application with an external vendor for outbound authentication.

values.name: platform_client
values.description: OAuth2 client credential for platform builders embedding Stigmer into their products.

values.name: team
values.description: Named group of an organization's people that access is shared with as one.

values.name: organization
values.description:
The boundary that holds people, Agents, Sessions and secrets
 together; nothing outside it sees them.

 Its id is a minted org_<ulid> that never changes; every organization-scoped
 resource names it by that id (metadata.org). Its slug is unique across the
 server and may change through rename; requests may name the organization
 by either.

values.name: platform
values.description: Singleton platform instance representing the Stigmer deployment.

values.name: agent
values.description: AI assistant with instructions, tools, skills, and a delegation model.

values.name: run
values.description: Single run of an agent within a session, tracking tool calls and responses.

values.name: session
values.description: Conversation thread between a user and an agent.

values.name: skill
values.description: Knowledge resource that provides domain-specific context to an agent.

values.name: agent_share
values.description: Hosted chat link for an agent with its own audience, origins, and credentials.

values.name: agent_channel
values.description: Connection binding an agent to an external messaging platform workspace.

values.name: channel_app
values.description:
Customer-owned messaging-platform app (e.g. a Slack app) that agent
 channels can install through instead of the shared platform app.

values.name: schedule
values.description: Recurring trigger that runs an agent on a cron schedule.

values.name: memory
values.description: Agent-proposed, user-confirmed fact the platform remembers about a person.

values.name: plugin
values.description:
An installed Agent Plugins package: one thing holding skills, agents,
 hooks and MCP servers, which agents and conversations list whole.

values.name: vault
values.description:
A person's or an organization's box of logins (matched by a tool's
 address) and secrets (matched by name) that runs use.

values.name: score
values.description:
One grade of a finished run: a person's thumbs or a free run-health
 check.

values.name: evaluator
values.description:
AI grading switched on for one agent: its sample rate, monthly spending
 limit and judge model.

values.name: plugin_eval
values.description:
One run of a plugin's own evals/ cases: every case tried with and
 without the plugin, on the models the eval names.

values.name: plan
values.description:
Catalog entry naming a bundle of entitlements and the terms that buy it.

 Platform-level: a plan belongs to no organization, so it carries no
 authorization scope and no owner. Immutable once created; a change of
 terms is a new Plan and the old one retires.

values.name: subscription
values.description:
An organization's binding to a Plan; at most one active per organization.

 System-created: the payment system drives its lifecycle, so it has no
 owner and grants no roles. Its reads and writes authorize on the
 organization through the billing permissions.

values.name: license
values.description:
A signed grant of entitlements to a self-hosting customer for a term.

 Platform-level: issued by the cloud's operators and verified offline by
 the Enterprise server, so the customer is a value inside the license
 (which may or may not name a cloud organization) and the kind has no
 authorization scope and no owner. Claims are immutable once signed; a
 renewal is a new License.

enumTypes.name: HookFormat
enumTypes.description: HookFormat is the hook format a plugin's hooks are written in.

values.name: HOOK_FORMAT_CLAUDE_CODE
values.description: Claude Code's hook format, also used by Codex plugins.

values.name: HOOK_FORMAT_CURSOR
values.description: Cursor's hook format.

enumTypes.name: PluginDialect
enumTypes.description:
PluginDialect names the manifest format a package was read from.

 Stigmer reads the open Agent Plugins format and the Cursor, Claude Code
 and Codex dialects unchanged; the dialect is recorded for display and
 support, never to branch behaviour after install.

values.name: PLUGIN_DIALECT_AGENT_PLUGINS
values.description: The open Agent Plugins format: a root plugin.json.

values.name: PLUGIN_DIALECT_CLAUDE
values.description: Claude Code: .claude-plugin/plugin.json.

values.name: PLUGIN_DIALECT_CURSOR
values.description: Cursor: .cursor-plugin/plugin.json.

values.name: PLUGIN_DIALECT_CODEX
values.description: Codex: .codex-plugin/plugin.json.

resourceDescription:
Plugin is an installed Agent Plugins package: one thing holding skills,
 agents, hooks and MCP servers, installed, upgraded and removed whole.

 Installing a plugin adds it to the organization and creates nothing else.
 An agent or a conversation lists the plugins it uses; a turn then gets
 every part of each, named under the plugin: its skills as
 <plugin>:<skill>, its agents as <plugin>:<agent>, its hooks, and its
 servers' tools.

statusType.name: PluginStatus
statusType.description:
PluginStatus is the system-managed state of an installed plugin: the
 archive identity and what the archive holds, read when the plugin was
 installed.

fields.name: Audit
fields.description: Standard audit information tracking creation and modification.

fields.name: Digest
fields.description: SHA-256 of the plugin archive, the immutable version identifier.

fields.name: ArtifactStorageKey
fields.description: Storage key of the plugin archive.

fields.name: Warnings
fields.description:
Warnings the last push recorded: components Stigmer does not carry,
 model hints it did not apply, names that shadow built-ins.

fields.name: Hooks
fields.description:
The plugin's tool-call hooks, as recorded at install; unset when the
 plugin carries none.

fields.name: Evals
fields.description:
The plugin's evals/ test cases, as read at install; unset when the
 plugin carries none.

fields.name: Skills
fields.description: The plugin's skills. A turn names each as <plugin>:<skill>.

fields.name: Agents
fields.description:
The plugin's agents, from its agents folder. A turn names each as
 <plugin>:<agent>.

fields.name: McpServers
fields.description: The plugin's MCP servers.

fields.name: Env
fields.description:
The variables the plugin's servers and hooks read, by name: the
 plugin's own declarations, a required secret for each name it uses but
 does not declare, and the login key of a server that signs in.

statusNestedTypes.name: ApiResourceAudit
statusNestedTypes.description: ApiResourceAudit contains both spec-level and status-level audit details.

fields.name: SpecAudit
fields.description: Audit info for the resource's specification (desired state).

fields.name: StatusAudit
fields.description: Audit info for the resource's status (actual state).

statusNestedTypes.name: ApiResourceAuditActor
statusNestedTypes.description:
ApiResourceAuditActor represents the entity that performed an action.

 This is the platform's single actor vocabulary: every "who did this"
 reference (created_by / updated_by, version-history applied_by / pushed_by,
 approval resolved_by_actor) uses this message, so actor rendering is
 uniform across all surfaces.

fields.name: Id
fields.description: Unique identifier of the actor.

fields.name: Avatar
fields.description: URL to the actor's avatar image.

fields.name: DisplayName
fields.description:
Human-readable display name (e.g. "Ada Lovelace"). Empty when unknown;
 renderers fall back to email, then id.

fields.name: Email
fields.description:
Email address of the actor. Empty when unknown or not applicable
 (e.g. machine accounts).

fields.name: PlatformClientId
fields.description:
The PlatformClient whose minted user token the actor acted through.
 Empty for every other credential, and on an actor that records no act
 (an account's profile lookup).

fields.name: CreatedBy
fields.description: Actor who created this resource.

fields.name: CreatedAt
fields.description: Timestamp when the resource was created.

fields.name: UpdatedBy
fields.description: Actor who last updated this resource.

fields.name: UpdatedAt
fields.description: Timestamp when the resource was last updated.

fields.name: Event
fields.description: Type of the last event (e.g., "created", "updated").

statusNestedTypes.name: EnvVarDeclaration
statusNestedTypes.description:
EnvVarDeclaration declares an environment variable a blueprint (an agent
 or an MCP server) needs, or optionally accepts.

 A declaration describes what the blueprint needs, never a person's or a
 deployment's value: a secret is found by its name in a vault when a run
 starts, and a plain setting that is the same wherever the blueprint runs
 may carry its value here.

fields.name: IsSecret
fields.description: Whether the value is a secret, found in a vault when a run starts.

fields.name: Description
fields.description:
Human-readable description shown where the value is asked for.
 Should explain what the variable is used for and where to obtain it.

fields.name: Optional
fields.description: Whether this variable is optional.

fields.name: Value
fields.description:
The fixed value of a setting that is not a secret and is the same
 wherever the blueprint runs, such as a log level or a response format.

 A value that differs per deployment, team or person (a workspace name,
 a host) belongs in a vault secret of the same name instead, which takes
 this value's place when a run starts.

statusNestedTypes.name: HookConfig
statusNestedTypes.description:
HookConfig is a set of tool-call hooks: commands that run before or after an
 agent's tool calls and can refuse a call, ask a person first, or let it run.

 A plugin's hooks are recorded here at install; an agent can also carry a
 block of its own (AgentSpec.hooks). Both engines, native and Cursor, run
 hooks in Claude Code's format (PreToolUse and PostToolUse) and in Cursor's
 (preToolUse, beforeShellExecution, beforeMCPExecution, postToolUse and
 afterMCPExecution).

fields.name: Format
fields.description:
The format the hooks are written in, which decides their input and answer.
 An agent's own block may leave it unset; Claude Code's format is assumed.
 A block in Cursor's format names it.

fields.name: Groups
fields.description: Hook groups, in the order they are declared.

statusNestedTypes.name: HookGroup
statusNestedTypes.description:
HookGroup is one event, an optional matcher, and the handlers that run when
 both match.

fields.name: Event
fields.description:
The event the handlers run on, spelled as the format spells it. In Claude
 Code's format: "PreToolUse" before a call, which can refuse it, ask first
 or allow it, or "PostToolUse" after a call succeeds, which can add to what
 the agent reads. In Cursor's: "preToolUse", "beforeShellExecution" (shell
 commands) and "beforeMCPExecution" (MCP tools) before a call, and
 "postToolUse" and "afterMCPExecution" (MCP tools) after one.

fields.name: Matcher
fields.description:
Which tools the handlers run for, in the format's own names. In Claude
 Code's format: a name such as "Bash", a list such as "Write|Edit", or a
 regular expression such as "mcp__github__.*"; a plugin's own MCP
 server's tools are named mcp__plugin_<plugin>_<server>__<tool>, as in
 Claude Code. In Cursor's: a regular expression tested against the tool's
 name ("Shell", "Write", "MCP:<tool>"), or, on "beforeShellExecution",
 against the command itself. Empty or "*" matches every tool.

fields.name: Handlers
fields.description: The handlers to run, in order.

statusNestedTypes.name: HookHandler
statusNestedTypes.description:
HookHandler is one command a hook runs.

 The command reads the call as JSON on stdin and answers as its format's
 hooks do: exit code 2 refuses the call, and JSON on stdout can allow, ask or
 deny with a reason. A Cursor-format "ask" waits for a person on both
 engines, where Cursor itself lets the call run.

fields.name: Command
Args
fields.description:
Arguments for the command's exec form; when set, the command runs without
 a shell. Claude Code's format only.

fields.name: TimeoutSeconds
fields.description:
Seconds the command may run before it is stopped; zero means the format's
 default, 600 seconds for Claude Code and 60 for Cursor. A command that is
 stopped makes no decision, unless fail_closed is set.

fields.name: Condition
fields.description:
A permission rule that narrows when the handler runs, e.g.
 "Bash(git push *)"; empty means whenever the group matches. Claude Code's
 format only.

fields.name: FailClosed
fields.description:
Whether a crash, timeout or missing answer blocks the call instead of
 letting it through. Cursor's format only.

statusNestedTypes.name: HttpMcpServer
statusNestedTypes.description: HttpMcpServer is an MCP server at an address.

fields.name: Url
fields.description: The server's URL.

fields.name: Headers
fields.description:
Headers sent with every request; a value may name a variable as
 ${NAME}.

fields.name: TimeoutSeconds
fields.description: Seconds to wait for one request; zero means the runner's default.

statusNestedTypes.name: McpServerEntry
statusNestedTypes.description:
McpServerEntry is one MCP server a plugin carries: a local program or an
 address.

fields.name: Name
fields.description:
The server's key in the plugin's MCP configuration. A turn names its
 tools mcp__plugin_<plugin>_<server>__<tool>, as Claude Code does.

fields.name: Stdio
fields.description: A local program the runner starts.

fields.name: Http
fields.description: A server at an address.

fields.name: Env
fields.description:
The names of the variables this server reads, declared in
 PluginStatus.env.

fields.name: SignIn
fields.description:
How a person signs in to this server; unset when it needs no sign-in or
 takes a key the plugin names.

statusNestedTypes.name: McpServerSignIn
statusNestedTypes.description: McpServerSignIn says how a person signs in to a server.

fields.name: OauthOnly
fields.description: Whether the server accepts only a sign-in, and no pasted key.

statusNestedTypes.name: PluginAgent
statusNestedTypes.description: PluginAgent is one agent a plugin carries, read from its agent file.

fields.name: Name
fields.description: The agent's name.

fields.name: Description
fields.description: What the agent specializes in.

fields.name: Instructions
fields.description: The agent's system prompt: the body of its file.

fields.name: Tools
fields.description:
Tools this agent may use, in Claude Code's names; empty means all of the
 turn's. Checked at install: an entry the agent's rules refuse is dropped
 with a warning, and an agent whose list loses every entry is left out.

fields.name: DisallowedTools
fields.description: Tools this agent may never use, in the same names as tools.

fields.name: Skills
fields.description: The plugin's own skills this agent uses, by name.

statusNestedTypes.name: PluginEvalSuite
statusNestedTypes.description: PluginEvalSuite summarises a plugin's evals/ test cases.

fields.name: Dir
fields.description:
The suite's directory relative to the plugin's root: "evals", or the
 manifest's experimental.evals.

fields.name: CaseCount
fields.description: Cases found in the suite.

fields.name: CaseTags
fields.description: The tags the listed cases carry, once each, sorted: at most 200.

fields.name: Cases
fields.description: Each case, in directory order.

fields.name: Findings
fields.description: Problems reading the suite: a case that cannot load, an unknown field.

statusNestedTypes.name: PluginEvalSuiteCase
statusNestedTypes.description: PluginEvalSuiteCase is one case of a plugin's eval suite.

fields.name: CaseName
fields.description: The case's name.

fields.name: Path
fields.description: The case's directory, relative to the plugin's root.

fields.name: CaseTags
fields.description: The case's tags.

fields.name: Unsupported
fields.description:
Why Stigmer cannot run the case yet, naming the feature, as in
 "context.scaffold_script"; empty when it can.

statusNestedTypes.name: PluginSkill
statusNestedTypes.description: PluginSkill is one skill a plugin carries.

fields.name: Name
fields.description: The skill's name, from its SKILL.md.

fields.name: Description
fields.description: What the skill is for, from its SKILL.md.

fields.name: Path
fields.description:
The skill's folder inside the plugin archive; empty when the plugin is
 one skill with SKILL.md at its root.

statusNestedTypes.name: PluginWarning
statusNestedTypes.description: PluginWarning is one thing a push noticed but did not refuse.

fields.name: Kind
fields.description:
Stable warning kind, e.g. "agent-not-installed", "component-ignored",
 "model-hint-unresolved", "settings-agent-not-applied",
 "tool-list-entry-dropped", "version-not-taggable".

fields.name: Message
fields.description: The warning as one user-facing sentence.

fields.name: Path
fields.description: The plugin-relative path the warning points at, when it has one.

statusNestedTypes.name: StdioMcpServer
statusNestedTypes.description:
StdioMcpServer is a local program serving MCP over its standard input and
 output.

fields.name: Command
fields.description: The program to run.

fields.name: Args
fields.description: Its arguments.
